title: Bread and Almond Dumplings in Tomato Sauce
subtitle: with parmesan and basil
description: Day-old challah is mashed with milk, ricotta, ground almonds and egg, shaped into patties, pan-fried and warmed through in a fresh tomato and chilli sauce.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 150°C and line a tray with baking paper. If the challah is not 3 days old, slice it, lay it on the tray and dry it in the oven for about 15 minutes.

Place the bread in a bowl, pour over the milk and mash by hand to a smooth paste. Add the ricotta, ground almonds, eggs, 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp salt, pepper and chopped basil and knead to an even mixture. Cover and refrigerate for about 1 hour.

Heat 1/2 cm of olive oil in a frying pan. With wet hands, shape small flat patties 3 to 4 cm wide and fry for 2 to 3 minutes each side until golden. Drain on paper towel. This can be done a day ahead.
For the sauce, prick the tomatoes all over with a fork, pack them into a bowl, sprinkle with 1 heaped tsp salt, cover and leave to release liquid for 30 minutes.
Transfer the tomatoes and their liquid to a food processor, add the basil leaves, garlic, chilli, 3 tbsp olive oil and brown sugar and blend until smooth. Taste and adjust the salt.
Pour the sauce into a wide, shallow pot and heat over medium heat to just below boiling. Add the dumplings and cook over low heat for a few minutes each side until hot and coated in sauce.
Drizzle generously with olive oil, scatter with grated parmesan and basil leaves and serve hot.
